title: Trading Venues, Market Structure and Infrastructure
summary: How regulated markets, multilateral and organised trading facilities and over-the-counter dealing differ, the transparency regime that supports price formation, and the supervision of central counterparties and securities depositories.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How regulated markets, multilateral and organised trading facilities and over-the-counter dealing differ, the transparency regime that supports price formation, and the supervision of central counterparties and securities depositories.
Learning Objectives: Distinguish venue types and their authorisation and rulebook requirements
Assess pre-trade and post-trade transparency and the use of waivers
Explain the Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures and their supervisory application
Syllabus: Regulated markets, multilateral platforms and dealing on own account
Transparency, dark trading and market fragmentation
Venue oversight: admission, rulebooks, surveillance and trading halts
Central counterparties, securities depositories and the PFMI
Intended Audience: Supervisors and inspectors responsible for brokers, investment advisers, portfolio managers and other investment firms
Market surveillance, market infrastructure and issuer disclosure staff
Policy specialists, team leaders and heads of department responsible for securities markets
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of supervising investment firms or securities markets is helpful. No trading or quantitative background is required.
Core Reading: IOSCO, Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation (2017)
CPMI-IOSCO, Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures (2012)
IOSCO, Regulatory Issues Raised by Changes in Market Structure (2013)
IOSCO, Compliance Function at Market Intermediaries (2006)
